svg.title: Apache Kafka
svg.desc: Apache Kafka. A partitioned, replicated commit log: producers append events, consumer groups read at their own pace and can replay history. Step 1, Where it sits: Orders appends OrderPlaced to topic orders; three consumer groups each read it at their own pace. Step 2, Append and replicate: Key C-14 picks P1. Leader b2 appends offset 42, b1 and b3 copy it, then acks=all confirms the write. Step 3, Consumer groups: One consumer per partition per group. billing commits 43, search-indexer lags at 39; a 4th idles. Step 4, Failover and the limits: b2 fails; in-sync b1 takes over P1, writes go on. Limits: order per partition, hot keys, retention.

g.text: Orders appends OrderPlaced to topic orders; three consumer groups each read it at their own pace.
Key C-14 picks P1. Leader b2 appends offset 42, b1 and b3 copy it, then acks=all confirms the write.
One consumer per partition per group. billing commits 43, search-indexer lags at 39; a 4th idles.
b2 fails; in-sync b1 takes over P1, writes go on. Limits: order per partition, hot keys, retention.
Records are appended in order and stay after they are read;
each group remembers its own position, its offset.
Inside, the topic is split into partitions, and every
partition is copied to several brokers.
its own offsets, read at its own pace
Reading a record doesn't remove it. Each group keeps its own position, so all three read every event at their own pace.
Records stay until retention.ms runs out (7 days here), so a group can fall behind, catch up, or replay from an earlier offset.
The key picks the partition: with 3 partitions, C-14 always lands on P1, so one customer's events stay in order. Only P1's leader takes writes.
b2 appends at offset 42, b1 and b3 fetch it, and with acks=all (the default since Kafka 3.0) the ack waits for every in-sync replica.
Each partition goes to one consumer per group, so 3 partitions keep at most 3 consumers busy. Each group commits its own offsets:
billing has read 42 and committed 43; search-indexer is at 39, 4 behind, and that is fine. Resetting offsets replays history.
b2 is down, but b1 and b3 are in sync and min.insync.replicas=2, so acks=all writes go on. The controller picked b1 from the ISR.
order holds only within a partition
a hot key overloads one partition
deleted after 7 days, or compacted to the latest per key
